title: A versatile polypharmacology platform promotes cytoprotection and viability of human pluripotent and differentiated cells.

experiments.model: Two hESC lines and three iPSC lines during cryopreservation/thawing
experiments.intervention: CEPT during thawing
experiments.comparator: DMSO vehicle in recovery culture, Y-27632, RevitaCell, CloneR, or SMC4; all groups had been cryopreserved
experiments.outcome_name: Live-cell fraction by calcein/PI imaging, confirmed by ATP assay
experiments.result: CEPT was reported as consistently superior during thawing across the tested cell lines and compared reagents.
experiments.sample_size: triplicate wells; 50,000 cells/well
experiments.evidence_excerpt: all five hPSC lines tested showed significantly improved viability

experiments.model: Cryopreserved iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, hepatocytes, astrocytes, and motor neurons
experiments.intervention: CEPT for 24 h after thawing
experiments.outcome_name: Survival and cardiomyocyte electrophysiology
experiments.timepoint: 24 h for survival; 5 days for electrophysiology
experiments.result: CEPT improved survival of differentiated cells after thawing and was evaluated for electrophysiological function in iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes. The separate motor-neuron MEA comparison in Extended Data Fig. 9 (day 7, n=3 wells, p=0.5023) does not establish significant functional superiority.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: Electrophysiological characterization of iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes 5 days post-thawing using multi-electrode arrays.

main_finding: CEPT improved post-thaw hPSC recovery and also supported differentiated-cell cytoprotection in the reported comparisons.
limitations: The excerpt does not establish that CEPT directly inhibits a single death pathway; several stress mechanisms were targeted together.

Formulation doses are captured; thermal handling and freezing-background allocation must still be resolved at the experiment level.
Extended Data Fig. 9 motor-neuron MEA at day 7 reports n=3 wells and p=0.5023; this does not establish significant neuronal functional superiority or equivalence.
Forebrain-neuron use with 2FA is a proposed transfer/combination test, not an already validated combination.
mechanism_claim: The study measured viability/recovery; multi-pathway stress protection is the authors' intervention rationale, while direct pathway causality is not established by recovery alone.

title: Cold Shock Protein B as an Alternative to DMSO for Oocyte Vitrification.
study_design: Recombinant cold shock protein B (CspB) was tested for ice control, DMSO replacement in mouse and bovine oocyte vitrification, developmental competence, and mTOR perturbation.
interventions: recombinant CspB from Polaribacter irgensii KOPRI 22228

experiments.model: CspB protein solutions in physiological saline
experiments.intervention: Recombinant CspB concentration series in sandwich recrystallization assay
experiments.cooling: quenching at −80 °C
experiments.warming: annealing at −20 °C; cryo-microscopy
experiments.outcome_name: Ice crystal size and recrystallization
experiments.timepoint: After annealing at −20 °C; duration not transcribed
experiments.result: The sandwich assay used 6 µL physiological saline samples quenched at −80 °C and annealed at −20 °C; ice crystal size decreased with CspB concentration. The reported recombinant Polaribacter protein was 21.9 kDa. GFP localization at the oocyte periphery/zona pellucida is not itself an ice-binding assay.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: inhibit ice crystallization and recrystallization

experiments.model: Mouse and bovine MII oocytes undergoing vitrification
experiments.intervention: Progressive DMSO/EG reduction with 1 or 2 mg/mL CspB; selected 15% EG + 2 mg/mL CspB
experiments.comparator: Standard 15% DMSO + 15% EG, 15% EG alone, and removal of both DMSO and EG
experiments.cooling: Five oocytes per vitrification carrier; rapid plunge into liquid nitrogen using commercial kit; thermal rate not reported
experiments.warming: Warming per commercial kit followed by 2 h recovery in mouse M16 or bovine maturation medium
experiments.outcome_name: Post-thaw survival and mouse developmental competence
experiments.timepoint: 2 h stabilization for mouse survival; cleavage 24 h and blastocyst 96 h post-activation
experiments.result: With 15% EG and no DMSO, mouse survival was 61.33 ± 3.69% without CspB (n=309), 72.93 ± 1.96% with 1 mg/mL (n=323), and 89.93 ± 1.20% with 2 mg/mL (n=352). Removing both DMSO and EG gave 3.97%, 7.00%, and 28.43% survival respectively. Bovine 15% EG + 2 mg/mL CspB survival was 87.53 ± 2.02% (n=101), versus 85.73 ± 2.55% for standard vitrification (n=121) and 46.87 ± 1.46% for EG alone (n=113). Mouse parthenogenetic cleavage/blastocyst outcomes were 91.82%/39.37% with CspB versus 93.04%/41.82% standard and 72.51%/24.13% EG alone; these are not live-birth outcomes.
experiments.sample_size: Mouse survival n=309/323/352 in reported 0% DMSO comparison; bovine n=101 CspB and n=121 standard vitrification; developmental subgroup n values reported by Figure 3
experiments.evidence_excerpt: significantly improved oocyte survival rates

experiments.model: Mouse MII oocytes vitrified in 15% EG + 2 mg/mL CspB
experiments.intervention: MHY1485 mTOR activator added before CspB vitrification; 5 or 10 μg/mL tested, 5 μg/mL selected
experiments.outcome_name: mTOR expression, ROS/GSH, mitochondrial function, and caspase-3/9 apoptosis markers
experiments.timepoint: post-vitrification quality assessment; 5 and 10 μg/mL activation screen
experiments.result: MHY1485 at 5 and 10 μg/mL upregulated mTOR; 5 μg/mL was selected. Adding the activator to CspB-treated oocytes increased oxidative stress, mitochondrial damage, and apoptosis markers, reversing the protective phenotype. This is pathway perturbation evidence, not direct CspB-mTOR binding evidence.
experiments.sample_size: Marker assays used groups of 15 oocytes for ROS/GSH/DHE and mitochondrial membrane-potential imaging; other assay n values vary by figure
experiments.source_locator: Methods 2.7–2.9; Results 3.6; Figure 5 and Supplementary Figure S1
experiments.evidence_excerpt: activation of mTOR abolished CspB’s beneficial effects

main_finding: Recombinant CspB reduced ice crystal injury and supported DMSO-reduced or DMSO-free mouse/bovine oocyte vitrification; mTOR activation reversed associated stress-marker protection.
limitations: This is mammalian reproductive transfer evidence, not human iPSC evidence.
Developmental outcomes and stress markers were assessed in mouse oocytes; bovine evidence in the extracted result is primarily survival.
mTOR perturbation supports pathway involvement but does not establish direct target binding or exclude upstream physical-injury effects.
CspB is a recombinant protein, not a small molecule; the reported 21.9 kDa Polaribacter construct should not be substituted with an unrelated protein sharing the CspB name.
The selected DMSO-free formulation retains 15% ethylene glycol. Removing both permeating CPAs yielded only 28.43% mouse survival even at 2 mg/mL CspB.
Survival is morphology/membrane-integrity scoring; oocyte counts are not independent donor or culture-run counts. Developmental endpoints follow parthenogenetic activation, not live birth.
Kit-based vitrification/warming does not specify a complete transferable thermal schedule. Protein sequence, tag and purity need confirmation before replication.
RNA methods refer to control and MBP groups; correspondence to the reported CspB groups requires clarification. No transcriptomic reanalysis was performed.
mechanism_claim: A sandwich ice assay measures physical ice control. Oocyte stress markers and mTOR-activator reversal support pathway involvement, but do not prove direct CspB-mTOR binding or selective inhibition. Ice-interface binding is modeled by molecular dynamics; GFP localization at the oocyte periphery/zona pellucida is a separate assay.
reviewer: Luna extraction; root selected methods/results review

Optimizer-stage DMSO recovery of 69.4% is a different comparator stage from final-validation recovery of 80.19%.

limitations: THP-1 is an immortalized monocytic leukemia line rather than primary monocytes; recovery, apoptosis and Raman assays have distinct denominators.

Polyampholyte chemistry is a modified poly(methyl vinyl ether-alt-maleic anhydride) starting from approximately 80 kDa material; exact composition/charge balance/lot specification matters, not any polymer labeled polyampholyte.
This is THP-1 monocytic leukemia-line evidence; three biological repeats are not three human donors.
Cryovials compare polyampholyte addition; plate experiments also add pollen-derived ice nucleator, so the plate gain cannot be attributed solely to polymer chemistry.
Cryo-Raman uses five individual cells per condition; text wording about percentages of cells should not be read as a population incidence estimate.
Post-thaw differentiation markers are supportive phenotype endpoints; no matched primary-monocyte/iPSC efficacy or comprehensive macrophage potency validation is established.
Storage demonstrated here is about 24 h at −80 °C; longer banking durability remains unverified in these experiments.
mechanism_claim: Cryo-Raman directly measured intracellular ice signatures; reduced apoptosis and improved recovery are biological outcomes associated with the formulation, not proof of a unique pathway.
